speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what measures are in place to promote the use of generic drugs in public healthcare institutions where they are assessed to be both cheaper and clinically equivalent to branded versions of the same drugs; (b) whether the Ministry tracks what proportion of the volume of all drugs prescribed are generics for those drugs where generic versions exist; and (c) if so, what is that figure in each of the last five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The utilisation of the generic drugs in the basket has risen over the years.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For one active ingredient that I just checked at retail, the cost difference is actually a factor of seven times.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, it can make a huge impact on curbing a spiraling healthcare cost.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is that something that the Government is looking into?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, again, anecdotally, there are cases that one hears about where in the private healthcare space, generic versions of drugs are sometimes prescribed at the same price as the branded version without the patient really being aware of it.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is this also something that the Government is looking at?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Lastly, is there a resource that patients can go to to access typical retail prices of branded versus generic drugs for common cases?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is this something that is available and, if not, can that be looked into as well?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We review them very regularly and these drugs are included because they have a high impact on the costs in terms of drug prescription.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Basically, these drugs are usually assessed to have high spending and high utilisation in the PHIs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the generic options at retail pharmacies, I think this will be up to the business model of the pharmacy in deciding whether it is better to bring in the generic options or the branded options.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, I have come across many private pharmacies that do carry generic options for patients' purchase.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will, hopefully, help reduce the cost of drugs in the private sector.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As they have different operational expenses and considerations, it is difficult for MOH to dictate exactly how much or what kind of drugs they prescribe to their patients.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: There was one question I asked: is there an online resource available for patients to check the price of generic versus clinically equivalent branded drugs, to educate patients so that they can perhaps demand for generic versions to lower the cost that they will need to bear?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And if such online resources are not available, is this something the Government is looking into?
